chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Musa from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
«The gift (hiba) is not permissible for anyone after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).»

key_terms.الْهِبَةُ: Gift, a voluntary transfer of property ownership without consideration
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.صَلَى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family, an honorific for the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on gift (hiba) after the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) declares that the 'gift' (hiba) is not permissible for anyone after the Messenger of Allah, a ruling often interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the exclusive and permanent gift of Wilayah or prophetic authority to the Ahl al-Bayt, which cannot be transferred to others. This establishes a theological boundary distinguishing the unique spiritual inheritance of the Prophet's family from general worldly transactions, emphasizing that the true 'gift' of divine guidance remains with them.
